signals.name: inactive_role_reallocation_delta
signals.market_scope: rushing yards, rush attempts, receiving yards, receptions, anytime TD, 2+ TD, longest rush, longest reception, passing yards (via protection/target loss)
signals.mechanism: When a starter is declared inactive ~90 minutes pregame, the offense must redistribute a fixed quantity of designed opportunity — carries, routes, red-zone snaps, protection assignments — to specific replacements. The replacement's opportunity changes discontinuously, not gradually, because opportunity is allocated by play design and personnel package, not by talent.
signals.point_in_time: T-90 minutes from kickoff at the earliest (official NFL inactive lists). A provisional version exists from the Friday final injury designation (Out/Doubtful) onward, i.e. ~T-48h for Sunday games. THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT INFORMATION STATES and must never share one signal key.
signals.historical_point_in_time_reconstructabil: POOR WITHOUT PROSPECTIVE ARCHIVAL. No free structured historical archive of official inactive lists with their publication timestamps was located. nflverse injuries carries a WEEKLY report/practice snapshot (verified columns: report_status, practice_status), not the T-90m inactive list. Reconstructing 'who was known out at T-90m' from final box scores is hindsight: a player absent from the box score may have been a late scratch or may have been out for three weeks. THIS IS THE PRIMARY JUSTIFICATION FOR NFL-01 PHASE A PROSPECTIVE ARCHIVAL.
signals.source: Official NFL/team inactive announcements (no machine-readable source established — Phase A records this verbatim as a known gap); ESPN summary?event=<id> per-team injuries block (verified present on scheduled events 2026-09-11); nflverse injuries_<season>.csv for the weekly designation layer
signals.access_method: For the weekly designation layer: bulk data package (nflverse release CSV). For the T-90m inactive list: NO automatable source established. Automation would have to read official team/league postings, which is a public page read whose terms are adverse (see terms_status). What automation would actually do: poll the archived weekly injury CSV plus ESPN's summary injuries block, and record NOT_CHECKED / UNAVAILABLE_BY_POLICY for the true inactive list.
signals.terms_status: SPLIT. nflverse bulk CSV: UNKNOWN-REQUIRES-REVIEW (no umbrella license found). Official nfl.com/team sources: PROHIBITED for automated harvesting — nfl.com Terms §1.3 verbatim: 'Systematic retrieval of data or other content from the Services, whether to create or compile, directly or indirectly, a collection, compilation, database, or directory, is prohibited absent our express prior written consent.' ESPN: Disney Terms of Use §2.B.x verbatim prohibits 'access, monitor, copy or extract the Disney Products using a robot, spider, script, or other automated means, including ... data mining or web scraping or otherwise compiling, building, creating or contributing to any collection of data, data set or database'.
signals.fragility: HIGH. The highest-value timestamp in NFL has no established machine-readable feed; every candidate route is either terms-adverse or an undocumented HTML/JSON surface that can change without notice.
signals.historical_depth: nflverse weekly injury layer: 2009-2024 documented, plus a live-verified 2026 asset (see fragility note in the source audit — the nflverse schedule page says the injury source 'died after the 2024 season' and 'there is no 2025 data', which CONTRADICTS the 200 OK on injuries_2026.csv observed 2026-09-11). Official T-90m inactive lists at point-in-time: ZERO archived depth prior to NFL-01 Phase A.
signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: HIGHEST IN THIS INVENTORY, as a hypothesis. The market unquestionably reprices the headline replacement (RB1 out -> RB2's line moves). The open question, and the reason this ranks first, is whether it correctly reprices the SECOND-ORDER consequences: the third-down back who now also takes the two-minute role, the TE whose route count rises because the offense shifts to 12 personnel, the slot receiver who inherits manufactured touches, the QB whose attempts rise because the run game is weaker. Those are separate FanDuel markets priced by the same books under time pressure.
signals.market_efficiency: PARTIAL AND ASYMMETRIC. Expect the primary replacement to be efficiently priced and the derived/secondary markets to be priced with a lag or by rule of thumb. This is an assertion to be measured, not a finding.
signals.volatility_risk: EXTREME BY CONSTRUCTION — this signal IS the volatility. A single additional inactive declared after the reading invalidates it. Any future implementation must carry the inactive-list vintage as part of the signal, not as metadata.

signals.name: goal_line_carry_share_change
signals.market_scope: anytime touchdown, 2+ touchdowns, rushing touchdowns, first/last TD scorer, team TD scorer markets
signals.mechanism: Rushing touchdowns are overwhelmingly produced from inside the 5, where carries are assigned by a specific goal-line personnel package rather than by the down-to-down rotation. A change in who takes those carries moves a player's TD probability far more than a change in his total carries, because the per-carry TD rate inside the 2 is an order of magnitude above the per-carry rate at midfield.
signals.point_in_time: Computable from the previous week's play-by-play the night after each game day (nflfastR pbp updates 'on a nightly basis after each game day'), so available from roughly T-5 days through kickoff. The reading is stale-but-known; it is not a pregame-news signal.
signals.historical_point_in_time_reconstructabil: GOOD. Derivable from prior-week pbp using yardline_100, goal_to_go, rush_attempt and rusher_player_id — all verified present in play_by_play_2026.csv. Reconstruction is clean PROVIDED the computation window is strictly capped at games completed before the prediction date. The leakage hazard is not the source, it is the window.
signals.source: nflfastR play-by-play via nflverse release asset play_by_play_<season>.csv (372 columns; verified 200, 2026 asset present with Week-1 opener only on 2026-09-11) — fields yardline_100, goal_to_go, rush_attempt, rusher_player_id, rush_touchdown, td_player_id (all verified present 2026-09-11)
signals.access_method: bulk data package (nflverse release CSV, ~98 MB per completed season; 333 KB for 2026 after one game). Automation would fetch the current-season pbp asset nightly, filter to games with gameday < prediction date, and aggregate inside-5 / inside-2 carries by player and team.
signals.terms_status: UNKNOWN-REQUIRES-REVIEW for the nflverse umbrella: no license statement was found on the nflverse data-update-schedule page. The FTN charting subset IS explicitly licensed: 'This data is released under the CC-BY-SA 4.0 Creative Commons license and attribution must be made to FTN Data via nflverse' (quoted from load_ftn_charting docs). Assets fetched 200 from GitHub release URLs with an honest self-identifying UA on 2026-09-11.
signals.fragility: LOW-MEDIUM. Documented, versioned release assets with a stated nightly cadence. Main risks are a naming change in the release tag and the fact that a mid-week re-run can silently include a Thursday game the prior run did not.
signals.historical_depth: 1999-present for pbp at play granularity; goal_to_go and yardline_100 present throughout the modern era of the dataset.
signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: HIGH. Anytime-TD is a heavily traded market, but its pricing tends to be driven by season-to-date TD counts and team implied total. A two-week-old change in goal-line rotation is a small-sample, high-leverage fact that season aggregates blur and that requires deliberate computation to see.
signals.market_efficiency: LIKELY INCOMPLETE. Books have the same play-by-play. The plausible inefficiency is not information asymmetry but shrinkage: a 4-carry inside-the-2 sample is genuinely ambiguous, and both sides must guess how much to update. That is a place where a measured, calibrated shrinkage could add value — and equally a place where a naive reading is pure noise.
signals.volatility_risk: HIGH. One inactive at RB, one short-yardage fumble, or one coaching decision to hand goal-line work to a fullback or QB invalidates it.

signals.name: alt_ladder_internal_coherence
signals.market_scope: all ALT and threshold ladders: PLAYER_X_ALT_PASSING_YARDS/RECEIVING_YARDS/RUSHING_YARDS/RECEPTIONS LOW-MEDIUM-HIGH, PLAYERS_WITH_10+/15+/20+/30+_YARDS_RECEPTION, TO_SCORE_2+/3+/4+_TOUCHDOWNS, RACE_TO_5/10/15/20/25/30
signals.mechanism: A ladder of thresholds on the same underlying quantity implies a full distribution. If the implied distribution is internally inconsistent, or inconsistent with the central line, the inconsistency is a pricing artefact rather than a football fact — and it is discoverable from the price sheet alone.
signals.point_in_time: Whenever the archive holds a full ladder for a player, i.e. any capture time.
signals.historical_point_in_time_reconstructabil: ONLY FROM FULL COUNT'S OWN ARCHIVE, same as all market signals.
signals.source: Full Count's own prospective FanDuel archive (nfl/archive, Phase A). VERIFIED from the 2026-09-11 capture: 262 FanDuel artifacts across 29 events and 8 tab slugs, 139 distinct marketType values, all CHECKED_AND_FOUND, captured from sbapi.nj.sportsbook.fanduel.com/api/event-page?eventId=<id>&tab=<slug>. The ladder density is unusually high: of the 139 observed marketTypes, a large share are ALT or threshold variants of the same quantity.
signals.access_method: derived from already-archived FanDuel payloads; no new acquisition.
signals.terms_status: UNKNOWN-REQUIRES-REVIEW. FanDuel's terms were NOT reviewed in this research pass and no legal conclusion is offered. Phase A already captures this source; the terms question is open and must be answered before any production dependency deepens.
signals.fragility: MEDIUM. Depends on ladder completeness in each capture, which depends on tab coverage, which has the silent-default failure mode described above.
signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: MEDIUM-HIGH AND UNUSUAL, BECAUSE IT DOES NOT REQUIRE PREDICTING FOOTBALL AT ALL. It requires only internal consistency of a price sheet, which is a strictly easier problem than forecasting a player's yards. It is also the one family here where Full Count's existing probability machinery (prop_probability.py, the pa_outcome_distribution precedent) transfers most directly.
signals.market_efficiency: This signal IS a test of market efficiency rather than an assumption about it. Where the ladder is coherent, there is nothing to find; where it is not, the finding is arithmetic.
signals.volatility_risk: LOW — it is a within-snapshot property and does not depend on any injury or role reading.
signals.prior_confidence: MEDIUM on the method, LOW on whether exploitable incoherence actually exists at FanDuel's pricing quality.

signals.name: contradiction_state_flag
signals.market_scope: all markets — this is an INFORMATION-RISK reading, not a directional football reading
signals.mechanism: When a head coach says a player is fine, the official report lists him Limited, and a credible beat reporter observes reduced work, the true state is not any one of those three: it is a state of elevated uncertainty about role and availability. Preserving the disagreement as its own reading is the only way the pipeline's confidence can reflect what is actually known.
signals.point_in_time: Continuous through the week; strongest Wednesday-Saturday. Requires at least two independent observations of the same entity within a validity window.
signals.historical_point_in_time_reconstructabil: ONLY VIA PROSPECTIVE ARCHIVAL, and only if each contributing observation is stored with its own first_observed timestamp and source. A contradiction cannot be reconstructed from a database that resolved it at write time. nfl/archive/provenance.py already reserves UNRESOLVED_CONTRADICTION as a first-class outcome, which is the correct foundation.
signals.source: Derived — a function over the archived intelligence corpus (official reports + coach media + beat observations), not an external feed
signals.access_method: derived from already-archived artifacts; no additional acquisition. Automation would compare claims about the same (player, field, week) across sources and emit the disagreement rather than a winner.
signals.terms_status: PERMITTED as a derived computation over artifacts Full Count already holds; inherits the terms_status of whatever sources contributed, which must be carried per-observation.
signals.fragility: MEDIUM. Depends entirely on multi-source coverage actually happening; with one source there are no contradictions to find, which would make silence look like agreement.
signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: HIGH, AND STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER ENTRY. This does not predict direction. It predicts that Full Count's own reading is less trustworthy than usual, which is actionable through abstention rather than through a pick. AGENTS.md #14 already requires that missing or stale data reduce confidence rather than become favorable evidence; this generalizes that rule to CONFLICTING data.
signals.market_efficiency: NOT APPLICABLE IN THE USUAL SENSE. A book does not post a price on 'the information is contradictory'. This is where a small independent system can rationally do better than a large one: by declining.
signals.volatility_risk: LOW — it is a reading ABOUT volatility.
signals.prior_confidence: LOW on any specific implementation; the design principle is inherited from shipped MLB behaviour rather than from measurement.

signals.name: coach_statement_role_claim
signals.market_scope: all player markets — primarily expected usage and availability
signals.mechanism: A coach's statement about a player's role ('more involved', 'full workload', 'committee', 'he'll get the goal-line work') is an announcement of intent by the person who allocates opportunity. If the statement is predictive of next-game snaps, routes, carries or red-zone usage, it is information about opportunity arriving before the opportunity exists.
signals.point_in_time: Continuously through the week from press conferences and media availability, typically Wednesday through Friday for a Sunday game, plus game-day pregame reports. AVAILABLE LIVE.
signals.historical_point_in_time_reconstructabil: POOR TO NONE WITHOUT PROSPECTIVE ARCHIVAL, AND THIS IS THE SHARPEST EXAMPLE OF THE ASYMMETRY THIS MISSION EXISTS TO FIX. Team transcript pages are current-facing; there is no verified structured historical corpus of coach statements with first-observed timestamps. Reconstructing 'what the coach said on Thursday' from a later article is unreliable and often circular. Statement-to-outcome measurement is ONLY possible on statements archived before the game they bear on.
signals.source: Official club transcript pages (verified to exist as public pages, e.g. patriots.com/news/transcripts and a Dolphins HC transcript page, both surfaced by search on 2026-09-11); official club and league video; NFL.com press-conference video channel
signals.access_method: public page read, WHICH IS TERMS-ADVERSE. Automation would have to fetch transcript pages systematically, which is exactly what the quoted clause prohibits. What automation would legitimately do instead: use WebSearch/WebFetch as a DISCOVERY layer to learn that a statement exists and what it said, record the source URL and the exact quoted span, and record the underlying transcript as UNAVAILABLE_BY_POLICY rather than bulk-harvesting it.
signals.terms_status: PROHIBITED for systematic automated retrieval. nfl.com Terms §1.3 verbatim: 'Systematic retrieval of data or other content from the Services, whether to create or compile, directly or indirectly, a collection, compilation, database, or directory, is prohibited absent our express prior written consent.' §11 verbatim prohibits use of 'any engine, software, tool, agent or other device or mechanism (including, browsers, spiders, robots, avatars or intelligent agents) to navigate or search the Services to harvest or otherwise collect information from the Services to be used for any commercial purpose.' Club sites operating under NFL terms inherit this; whether each club site's own terms differ is UNKNOWN-REQUIRES-REVIEW.
signals.fragility: HIGH. Terms-adverse acquisition, no stable structure, per-club page layouts, and the content is natural language whose extraction is model-dependent and versioned.
signals.historical_depth: ZERO archived at point-in-time before NFL-01. Club transcript archives exist as web pages but were not established as retrievable in bulk under acceptable terms.
signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: HIGH AS A HYPOTHESIS AND EXPLICITLY UNMEASURED. Jacob's requirement that coach and player press conferences be reviewed every day is a product and scientific requirement, and this signal is its signal-level expression. BUT: COACH SPEECH IS NOT GROUND TRUTH. Coaches are strategically vague, sometimes wrong, and occasionally deliberately misleading. Nothing here may be promoted on the basis that a coach said it.
signals.market_efficiency: UNKNOWN AND PROBABLY HETEROGENEOUS BY SPEAKER. A widely reported quote from a prominent head coach is in the price within minutes. A position coach's remark in a local availability may not be. That heterogeneity is the measurable object.
signals.volatility_risk: HIGH. A statement is superseded by the Friday designation and again by the T-90m inactive list.
signals.prior_confidence: LOW. NOTHING may be HIGH on coach-quote grounds alone, and this entry is the canonical case.

A player's share of his team's end-zone targets is a narrower and more causal TD-opportunity measure than red-zone target share, because a red-zone target short of the goal line rarely produces a touchdown.

The leakage risk is the aggregation window, not the source; a future engine must enforce it the way backtest/engine.py's PointInTime class and verify_no_lookahead() already do for MLB. Identifiable from yardline_100 and air_yards: a target whose air yards reach or exceed the distance to the goal line is an end-zone target. Both fields verified present.

signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: MEDIUM-HIGH. It requires a derivation rather than a lookup, it is the tightest available proxy for designed TD intent, and it feeds the single-underlying-opportunity-model architecture that the TD family requires.

signals.name: speaker_reliability_profile
signals.market_scope: meta-signal: modulates the weight of every coach_statement_role_claim reading
signals.mechanism: Different speakers are differently informative. A profile built per (speaker, staff, claim category) from archived statement-to-outcome pairs answers whether THIS coach's 'he'll be more involved' has historically preceded a measurable increase in snaps, routes, carries or red-zone usage. Reliability is an empirical property of a speaker, not an assumption.
signals.point_in_time: Derived; available whenever the archive supports it. Requires many archived statement-outcome pairs before it exists at all.
signals.historical_point_in_time_reconstructabil: ONLY PROSPECTIVELY, BY CONSTRUCTION. A reliability profile computed on statements retrieved after their games is contaminated by selection: the statements that survive in accessible form are disproportionately the ones that turned out to matter.
signals.source: Derived from Full Count's own archived intelligence corpus joined to nflverse snap_counts / pbp outcomes
signals.access_method: derived; no external acquisition
signals.terms_status: PERMITTED as a derived computation; inherits per-observation terms from the contributing sources.
signals.fragility: MEDIUM. Depends on sustained archival breadth; a profile built on one club's coverage generalises to nothing.
signals.historical_depth: ZERO. Cannot exist until statements have been archived across many weeks.
signals.expected_marginal_info_beyond_market: POTENTIALLY HIGH AND STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE TO CASUAL ACTORS. This is the clearest place where patient prospective archival could produce something a faster, larger operation does not bother to build. IT IS ALSO WHERE OVERCONFIDENCE IS CHEAPEST: with ~17 games a season and a few dozen statements per coach, a reliability estimate will be desperately underpowered for years. RECORD FIRST, MEASURE LATER, PROMOTE ONLY IF EVIDENCE WARRANTS.
signals.market_efficiency: Not a priced quantity.
signals.volatility_risk: LOW as a profile; but a coaching change destroys the profile it was built on, which is a severe practical limit given NFL staff turnover.
signals.prior_confidence: LOW. Explicitly: DO NOT assume all coaches are equally informative, and DO NOT assume specificity implies usefulness — a very specific claim can be a very specific error.

signals.name: ol_configuration_change
signals.market_scope: passing yards, completions, sacks (opposing), rushing yards, rush attempts, interceptions thrown
signals.mechanism: Offensive line continuity affects protection quality and run-lane creation for the entire offense at once. signals.mechanism: Touchdowns require red-zone possessions. The number of red-zone trips a team gets is the population from which all its scoring props are drawn, and it is driven by expected team points and drive success rather than by any individual's ability.

Reading it later yields the CLOSING line, not the line at the prediction cutoff. This is the identical failure mode as MLB's team_total_open/team_total_move, which measure_signals.py names as permanently forward-only.

markets.base_rate: Computed from 2025 pbp solo_tackle_1/2 and assist_tackle_1..4 player ids. Pool = defender-games with >=1 combined (n=11,025): over 2.5: 49.1%; over 3.5: 35.1%; over 4.5: 25.1%; over 5.5: 17.1%; over 6.5: 11.4%; over 7.5: 7.7%; over 8.5: 5.0%. Restricting to defender-games with >=4 combined (n=3,872), over 5.5 = 48.7%, which is closer to how a book would select its posting pool.
markets.typical_line: NOT OBSERVED ON FANDUEL. markets.settlement_nuance: MAJOR SETTLEMENT NUANCE. Tackle statistics are NOT officially standardised the way yardage is: solo and assisted tackles are assigned by scorers and differ between the official gamebook and third-party sources. Any tackles market must be settled against a NAMED source, and grading it from nflfastR pbp would be grading against a different source than the book uses. That is precisely the class of bug Full Count's MLB grading_sources.py exists to control.

markets.base_rate: Computed from 2025 pbp: 998 player-games with >=1.0 full sack across 272 games, i.e. 3.67 per game league-wide. Against a denominator of defender-games with >=20 defensive snaps (7,809 from snap_counts_2025) the implied rate is 12.8%; restricted to front-seven positions with >=20 snaps (4,813) it is 20.7%. These are ratios of independently computed counts, not a row-level join (gsis and pfr id systems differ), so they are rate ESTIMATES.
markets.typical_line: TO_RECORD_1+_SACK observed live, plus a 'To Record a Sack Parlay Builder' tab title in the NFL root page.
markets.settlement_nuance: HALF SACKS ARE THE CENTRAL NUANCE. Two players splitting a sack are each credited 0.5, which at most books does NOT satisfy a 1+ sack market. Any grading must decide and document whether 0.5 counts, and 17.6% of the sack player-games in this 2025 sample were half-sacks only (1,211 player-games with >=0.5 versus 998 with >=1.0).

markets.typical_line: Near-coinflip around 7.5-8 points. On FanDuel these appear as TEAM-level selections inside GAME_SPECIALS_-_KICKING with verified runner names 'BUF Bills 7+ Total Kicking Points', 'BUF Bills 10+ Total Kicking Points', 'BUF Bills 12+ Total Kicking Points' — NOT as an individual kicker market in the sampled slate.
markets.settlement_nuance: Kicking points = 3 per field goal + 1 per extra point. A missed extra point or a blocked kick costs a point. A TEAM total-kicking-points market also captures a second kicker after an injury, whereas a player market would not — a real difference in what is being bet.

markets.settlement_nuance: A field goal negated by penalty and re-kicked counts once. A field goal attempt on the final play of a half still counts. The 2+ made-FG market is strongly NEGATIVELY related to the same team's touchdown markets: red-zone trips convert to one or the other, which is a within-game negative correlation correlation.py's label scheme would classify explicitly.
